answer: Each agent runs inside a TEE and signs the epoch quote with its enclave key. The quote binds the binary hash, so a cloned runtime yields a different measurement. Duplicate detection replays the submitted text against the recorded inputs and flags identical output regardless of label. Every unverified claim cuts the score by 1 point, and 5 points drop the identity from the jury pool. A farm needs real enclaves, and 1,000 of them cost 1,000 attestations plus forge time. Nectar does not cover that bill, and the canyon between honest and cloned hardware is the whole defense.
